# Workflows that declare workflow_dispatch but are not yet on the
# default branch (#644), enforced by scripts/check-dispatch-reachable.sh.
#
# `schedule` IS SUBJECT TO THE SAME RESTRICTION AND THIS FILE USED TO BE
# SILENT ABOUT IT (#846). The restriction is a property of the DEFAULT
# BRANCH, not of one trigger: a workflow that is not on `main` does not
# run on a cron either.
#
# What the record actually shows, walked commit by commit on 2026-08-27
# rather than recalled. Two entries asserted that the cron survives off
# the default branch, in different words, eleven minutes apart:
#
#   0917847, 12:51:56, for fork-execution-policy.yml --
#     "It runs on a daily schedule from the moment it merges, so the
#      schedule half works immediately"
#   5257600, 13:02:37, for run-retention.yml --
#     "The workflow's real trigger is the daily schedule, which works
#      from any branch"
#
# Three corrections to how that was first written up here, because a
# paragraph telling the next author to measure rather than reason is the
# worst possible place for an unmeasured claim:
#
#   - It said both entries were written independently BY TWO AUTHORS.
#     Nothing in the record says that. Both commits carry the same single
#     identity as author and committer.
#   - It set off "the schedule works from any branch" in quotation marks
#     as what they said. That exact string is in neither. The two real
#     sentences are quoted above.
#   - It said "two entries HERE". Only one of them was ever on the merged
#     line of development: 5257600's. The other lives on the #830
#     settings-guard branch, where it was corrected before merge. This
#     file, on `dev`, has carried exactly one such entry, ever. A claim
#     true of the union of the branches in flight is not a claim about
#     this file.
#
# So: if you are writing a reason below, do not reason about which
# trigger survives. Measure it -- and the `Triggers:` line the gate now
# requires is derived from your workflow rather than from your sentence.
#
# GitHub only exposes a dispatchable workflow from the DEFAULT branch.
# This project develops on `dev` and releases to `main`, and `main` is
# the default, so a new dispatch-only workflow is undispatchable for one
# release cycle after it merges. That is normal; being undispatchable
# and DOCUMENTED AS A ROUTE is not.
#
# Rules. EACH ONE CARRIES ITS OWN ENFORCEMENT CLASS, and the class is
# checked rather than asserted. The first version of this header said
# "the gate enforces all of them"; one of the four rules below was
# enforced by nothing at all, in the very PR whose subject was claims
# in this file that are wider than the code behind them.
#
#   [enforced: id]   a case in scripts/test-check-dispatch-reachable.sh
#                    drives a violation of that rule and requires the
#                    gate to FAIL.
#   [unenforced: id] a case drives the violation and observes the gate
#                    PASS. It is an obligation on the author, and the
#                    case exists to pin the boundary: if someone makes
#                    the gate enforce it, that case goes red and this
#                    tag has to be changed with it.
#
# The suite reads these tags back out of this file and demands one
# driven case per tag, of the matching polarity. So the classes cannot
# drift from what the gate does, and moving a rule into [enforced:]
# without writing the code goes red.
#
# THE DOMAIN OF THAT CHECK, AND ITS ONE ESCAPE, STATED HERE RATHER THAN
# DISCOVERED LATER. The suite sees a rule as an INDENTED LIST ITEM in
# this block, and nothing else: `#`, whitespace, one of `-` `*` `+`,
# then whitespace. A rule written that way cannot be added without
# declaring its class -- all three checks cover it, and a case drives
# each of the three markers separately.
#
# Written any other way, a rule is invisible to all three. The domain
# cannot simply be "every line in the block", because CONTINUATION
# LINES are part of this format -- every rule below has them -- and a
# rule written with no marker is indistinguishable from a continuation
# of the rule above it. That specific escape is the one that cannot be
# closed by a better pattern; a merely malformed marker could be, and
# if one ever turns up the pattern is the place to fix it, not this
# paragraph.
#
# So the escape is pinned by a case that asserts the miss, exactly as
# [unenforced: docs-say-unavailable] is pinned below. If anyone ever
# makes an unmarked rule detectable, that case goes red and this
# paragraph has to change with it.
#
# This replaces an unqualified "a new rule cannot be added without
# declaring which class it is in". That was false for `*`, for `+`, and
# for an unmarked line -- written into the guard built to stop this
# file from making claims wider than its code, which is the fourth time
# a fix here has carried the defect class of its own finding. The
# remedy for the marker half was a wider pattern; the remedy for the
# unmarked half is this paragraph plus a case, not a wider sentence.
#
#   - [enforced: reason-and-clears]
#     An entry requires a reason and what clears it. No bare paths.
#     A bare path used to pass byte-identically to a full entry.
#   - [enforced: derived-triggers]
#     An entry requires `Triggers:`, listing every default-branch-only
#     trigger the workflow actually declares. The gate DERIVES that list
#     from the workflow file and requires an exact match, in both
#     directions -- an entry that omits `schedule` fails, and so does one
#     that claims `schedule` for a workflow that has none. It is keyed on
#     the file's triggers, never on the wording of the reason, because
#     both of the false entries in #846 were fluent English.
#   - [unenforced: docs-say-unavailable]
#     The documentation for the workflow must say it is not available
#     yet, for as long as the entry is here. NO CODE CHECKS THIS. The
#     gate never opens a document; the only documentation it ever
#     mentions is the advisory block it prints for an UNDECLARED
#     workflow, which says nothing about a declared one. A
#     tree with a complete, truthful entry here and a doc page naming
#     the 404-ing workflow as its primary route passes today, which is
#     exactly the #665 failure this ledger exists for. It is the same
#     boundary check-dispatch-reachable.sh already states for the
#     reason field: a mechanical check cannot tell a true sentence from
#     a fluent invented one, and it cannot tell a documented route from
#     a filename that merely appears in a document.
#   - [enforced: stale-entry-pruned]
#     The gate fails when an entry stops being needed — the workflow
#     reached the default branch, so remove the entry. An allowlist
#     nobody prunes is how a temporary exception becomes permanent.
#     A pull request INTO the default branch counts as reaching it
#     (#977): merging that pull request is what puts the workflow
#     there, so the entry is stale ON the pull request, and the release
#     PR is where it gets removed. Removing it after the release
#     instead is what turned this gate red on the default branch at
#     v2.1.0, one commit after the merge.
#     The removal reaches that pull request by riding the release
#     branch into `dev` first, so for the length of the release the
#     entry is GONE from `dev` while the workflow is still absent from
#     the default branch. The gate reads that state from the version
#     pins, and from nothing else: while this tree pins the immediate
#     successor of what the default branch pins, a missing entry is
#     taken as the removal in transit. Four bounds come with that, and
#     they are the written expiry this ledger demands of its own
#     entries:
#     FIRST, the gate cannot tell a release from a bare pin bump. It
#     never looks for a release branch, a pruned entry or a release
#     pull request, and check-version-pins.sh permits a tree to lead
#     the latest tag, so a bump on any branch suspends the finding the
#     same way. Every run it applies to says so in its own output.
#     SECOND, while suspended the finding is off for EVERY dispatchable
#     workflow, so one merged undeclared in that window is not caught
#     until the pins agree again.
#     THIRD, the bound is a DISTANCE, not a duration. The suspension
#     holds while this tree pins the immediate successor of the default
#     branch, and two steps apart is refused. Nothing in the gate reads
#     a clock, a tag or the state of a release, so a release parked
#     after runbook step 5 sits exactly one step ahead and stays
#     suspended for as long as nobody finishes or unwinds it.
#     FOURTH, one step and only ahead. A release that skips a version, a
#     release cut on an older line, and a tree that is simply behind are
#     all outside it, and on those the #977 deadlock is back: the
#     release pull request needs the entry, and the pull request that
#     removes it is red. "A release moves the version one step" is a
#     convention of this project, not an invariant. Every run that
#     REPORTS an undeclared workflow while the pins differ says the
#     suspension did not apply, names both pins and the readings that
#     arm allows, and names an entry here as the way through. A run
#     with nothing to report stays quiet, pins or no pins.
#     The stale rule is never suspended.
#
